content:
Texas A&M International University will host its second biannual LEARN Expo on Wednesday, Nov. 18, from 3:20 to 4:20 p.m. in the Student Center Ballroom, where 109 student groups will present the hands-on learning projects they have worked on, according to the university.

The event is free and open to the public. Visitors can vote for their favorite poster, which will receive a special prize alongside the top three judge-scored posters, according to TAMIU.

The student presentations will cover undergraduate research projects, internship experiences, service learning and more, according to the university.

QEP-LEARN director Cihtlalli G. Perez said the expo centers on students and their experiences, giving them a platform to showcase work they often complete alongside peers engaged in hands-on learning at the university.

The expo is part of TAMIU's 10-year Quality Enhancement Plan, known as LEARN — Learning Experientially: Active Real-world Navigation — which focuses on experiential learning, according to the university.

Sources: Texas A&M International University.

title: TAMIU to Host Second LEARN Expo Nov. 18, With 109 Student Groups Presenting
